name: Levant Red
lede: Levant red is an alternative name for Turkey red, a brilliant alizarin red dye used in Britain from 1785 into the 1930s.

sections.title: Another name for Turkey red
sections.body:
Paterson sends Levant red straight to Turkey red [1]. The Turkey red entry calls it a brilliant red dye made from alizarin, described as yellowish red, a moderate red or a brownish red, and also called Adrianople red [2]. Paterson also defines "Turkey" as originating from Turkey or the Levant [2].

Paterson says the technique of dyeing cloth and yarn this way was extensively practised in Britain between 1785 and the 1930s [2].

sections.title: Where it sits
sections.body: Paterson's index lists Levant red among the reds [3]. The colour belongs in the reds beside [[madder]] and shades such as [[light-red]] and [[indian-red]] [4]. Whatever it is called, Paterson's wording shows the range one dye can cover, from yellowish to brownish red [2]. The swatch is a muted, brick-leaning red [4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No usable archive measurements exist for this name, so there is no painting data to quote [4].
